## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)
**System Name:** Main House
**Maintenance Interval:** 12 months

## SYSTEM STATUS
**CRITICAL ISSUE IDENTIFIED.** This maintenance visit recorded a critical pump fault requiring immediate professional attention. The effluent pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its nameplate amperage, indicating no hydraulic load. This condition poses an immediate risk of motor damage from overheating without fluid cooling. All other components are in good condition and the dispersal field is dry with no surface breakout.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

## COMPONENT ASSESSMENT
| Component | Condition | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary Tank | Good | Concrete, 1250-gallon capacity |
| Effluent Filter | Good | Light soiling; cleaned and reseated during this visit |
| Liquid Level | At Outlet | Normal operating level |
| Dispersal Field | Good | Surface dry; no breakout observed |
| High Water Alarm | Functional | Tested and confirmed operational |
| Electrical Connections | Sound | No corrosion or loose terminals |

## PUMP ASSESSMENT -- CRITICAL FINDING
**Pump Current Draw: 1.6A measured / 7.2A nameplate = 22.2% FLA -- CRITICAL - No Load**

The effluent pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its rated amperage. This indicates the pump is operating without hydraulic load. The most likely causes are:
- Broken or missing impeller
- Severed or disconnected discharge line
- Dry-run condition (no fluid reaching the pump inlet)

A pump running without load generates heat without the cooling effect of fluid circulation. Continued operation risks motor burnout and failure.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**IMMEDIATE (Critical Priority)**
- **Immediate professional attention required.** A qualified technician must examine the pump discharge line for disconnection or damage, and must check the pump impeller for breakage or obstruction. Do not continue operating the system until the pump load condition is resolved. Continued operation risks permanent motor damage.

**Routine Maintenance**
- Continue the current 12-month maintenance interval once the pump fault is corrected and normal operation is restored.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### Pump Failure Risk
Your pump is running but not moving water. This is a serious condition that will damage the motor if left unaddressed. The pump needs immediate attention from a qualified technician. Do not delay.

### Tank Solids
This maintenance visit recorded solids at 22.9 percent of tank volume, which is within the normal range. Solids accumulate naturally over time. Keeping non-biodegradable material out of the system -- wipes, paper towels, cooking grease -- keeps that accumulation slow and predictable.
